key_themes: Nvidia earnings beat drives AI/data center stocks higher in after-hours trading
Broad market selloff: S&P 500 hits lowest close since July, Dow down 1.6%
Managed care stocks under pressure; software names weakest sector

stocks.discussion_driver: Nvidia reported Q3 FY2027 earnings after the bell, crushing estimates: EPS of $2.68 vs $2.47 expected and revenue of $115.8B (up 103% YoY) vs $108.8B estimated. Q4 guidance of $127.4B-$132.6B also beat expectations. The report was the first earnings call led by interim CEO Colette Kress following Jensen Huang's departure, sending shares up 4%+ in after-hours trading despite a -36% drawdown from the 52-week high.
bull_case: Dominant AI chip market share with Blackwell GPU demand driving 103% YoY revenue growth; data center infrastructure spending shows no signs of abating with hyperscalers committing to record capex
Q4 guidance of $127-$132.6B signals continued acceleration, and analyst consensus target of $265 implies 70%+ upside from current levels reflecting long-term earnings power
bear_case: CEO transition risk: Jensen Huang stepping back introduces leadership uncertainty at a pivotal time for AI chip competition, with AMD and custom silicon from Google and Amazon gaining ground
Stock has fallen 36% from its 52-week high of $243.37 amid broader tech selloff; valuation compression could continue if macro headwinds persist

stocks.discussion_driver: SELLAS shares surged approximately 156% on November 17 after the company reported a positive result from its cancer vaccine trial, specifically for leukemia treatment using its GPS immunotherapy platform. The stock opened at $24.00, hit a high of $24.89, and closed at $19.15 on volume of 119.5 million shares (vs. typical ~4-8M), setting a new 52-week high and vaulting past the prior high of $15.88.
bull_case: Positive Phase 3 cancer vaccine trial result validates the GPS platform as a credible leukemia treatment; breakthrough data could accelerate FDA approval pathway and attract partnership interest from large pharma
Analyst consensus price target of $32.50 implies an additional 70% upside from current post-surge levels, with top-line targets as high as $35 (Alliance Global Partners)
bear_case: Binary biotech risk: additional trials and FDA approval remain uncertain; a single positive data readout does not guarantee regulatory clearance or commercial success
Very thin analyst coverage (only 2 analysts tracked) and small market cap make the stock highly volatile; after-hours retracement to $16.90 from the $19.15 close suggests risk of further pullback

stocks.discussion_driver: AECOM surged approximately 12.7% on November 17 after issuing FY2027 EPS guidance of $6.15-$6.35, well above analyst expectations. The engineering and infrastructure giant reported fiscal Q4 results on November 16, with the positive guidance driving a gap-up open the following session. Shares rose from a Nov 16 close of $72.50 to approximately $82.50 on strong volume.
bull_case: FY2027 EPS guidance of $6.15-$6.35 signals management confidence in infrastructure spending tailwinds from U.S. government infrastructure programs and global construction demand
Moderate Buy consensus with $86.63 average target still implies ~5% upside even after the sharp gap-up; infrastructure spending is a durable multi-year theme
bear_case: Stock is now 38.6% below its 52-week high of $134.36, suggesting the broader trajectory has been negative; the gap-up may face resistance as the stock was recently trading in the low $70s
Government contracting exposure means revenue can be lumpy and subject to budget cycles; any federal spending cuts or policy shifts could impact future project pipelines

stocks.discussion_driver: Red Cat Holdings was the biggest decliner of the November 17 session after reporting Q3 results that badly missed estimates: revenue of $20.19M came in approximately 71% below the consensus estimate of $39.51M. The company also withdrew its full-year 2026 revenue target of $150M-$180M. The stock fell ~32% on the day. Three analysts cut price targets sharply: HC Wainwright ($20→$10), Needham ($15→$5), and Piper Sandler ($6→$3).
bull_case: Long-term defense drone demand remains secular; Red Cat is positioned in the growing U.S. military small drone market and could recover if it wins new government contracts
HC Wainwright maintained a Buy rating with a $10 target despite the cut, implying over 300% upside potential from current levels for high-risk investors
bear_case: Revenue contracted 42% sequentially to $11.8M and the company withdrew annual guidance entirely, eliminating near-term earnings visibility and destroying credibility with investors
52-week high was $18.78; current price of $2.41 represents an 87.2% drawdown with no clear catalyst for recovery in the near term

stocks.discussion_driver: Disney reported fiscal Q4 2026 results on November 17 that beat on both top and bottom lines: revenue of $25.9B (up 16% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.77 vs $1.11 a year ago (+59% YoY). Total segment operating income jumped 43% to $4.97B. The company declared a $2.00/share dividend and reiterated double-digit earnings growth for FY2027. Despite the beat, shares fell ~1.47% to $116.96 as broad market selling pressure overwhelmed the positive news.
bull_case: 43% jump in operating income and reiterated double-digit growth guidance for FY2027 demonstrates successful transformation of the streaming and parks businesses under CEO Bob Iger
$2.00/share dividend declaration adds income appeal and signals strong free cash flow generation; analyst consensus of $127.54 implies ~9% additional upside
bear_case: Stock closed lower despite a clear earnings beat, reflecting the challenging macro environment and potentially signaling that good news is already priced in near the 52-week high
Intense streaming competition from Netflix, Amazon, and Apple continues to pressure subscriber growth and content spending requirements
